2608.28058.title: Dynamic Alignment Compensation for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
2608.28058.paper_summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) remain prone to hallucinations, producing responses that are irrelevant or inconsistent with the multimodal input. Existing mitigation methods mainly rely on external supervision, output calibration, or attention regulation, leaving the internal representation dynamics of autoregressive generation underexplored. We identify an inference-time failure mode in which cross-modal representations degrade across decoder layers and drift across generation steps, destabilizing token prediction and increasing hallucination risk. We propose \emph{Dynamic Alignment Compensation} (DAC), a training-free inference-time method that detects representation divergence and selectively applies lightweight residual compensation. DAC combines Layer-wise Semantic Compensation to mitigate inter-layer degradation with Sequential Semantic Correction to constrain temporal drift. Experiments on nine hallucination-focused and general-purpose multimodal benchmarks across multiple LVLM backbones show that DAC consistently reduces hallucinations while maintaining strong overall performance.
2608.28058.paper_summary_zh: 大型視覺-語言模型（LVLMs）仍然容易產生幻覺，生成與多模態輸入無關或不一致的回應。現有的緩解方法主要依賴於外部監督、輸出校準或注意力調節，導致自回歸生成的內部表示動態未被充分探索。我們識別出一種推理時的失敗模式，其中跨模態表示在解碼器層之間退化並在生成步驟中漂移，這不穩定了標記預測並增加了幻覺風險。我們提出了\emph{動態對齊補償}（DAC），這是一種無需訓練的推理時方法，能檢測表示的發散並選擇性地應用輕量級的殘差補償。DAC結合了逐層語義補償以減輕層間退化，並使用序列語義校正來限制時間漂移。在九個專注於幻覺的和通用多模態基準測試中，跨多個LVLM骨幹的實驗顯示，DAC始終能減少幻覺，同時保持強大的整體性能。
